findings.summary: Only the blue solved traces are visible in all three panels of the 1714x882 render. The figure's own legend declares four series (render.py:74-81), but the black dashed 'EFIT-coordinate source' has no visible ink in any panel and the dotted 'EFIT map' survives only as a several-pixel sliver near radius 0.2 m (total current) and near 1.35 m (pressure). The solved trace is drawn last at 3 pt over a 2.6 pt reference (render.py:53-59), so the reader cannot tell whether the reference coincides exactly with the solved trace -- what a converged control would do -- or is absent from the saved bank. The figure exists to show the solved-against-EFIT comparison, and that comparison cannot be read. Remedy: draw the reference so it stays distinguishable when it coincides (dash offset or a thin line stepped just off the solved trace).

The axis and null markers carry no key. The panels draw solved critical points as circles, reference critical points as squares and both null sets through draw_nulls (render.py:143-160), but the figure legend names only solved, EFIT and wall (render.py:164-172) and the only caption text is the contour-level list (render.py:176-181). The nova poloidal rule requires the panel to say which null set is which; here a reader cannot tell which marker is the magnetic axis and which the admitted X-point, nor which set belongs to the solved field and which to EFIT. At 6 pt the two sets also overplot near the core, so the distinction is not recoverable by inspection.

Same defect as the 137D poloidal panel: the axis and null markers have no legend entry or caption explanation (render.py:143-172, 176-181), and the solved and reference marker sets overplot near the core at 6 pt, so which marker is the axis and which the admitted X-point cannot be determined by a reader.

The MAST panel autoscales its y-axis to 0.465-0.575 MA/m2 while 137D runs 0.0-1.9 and 146D 0.0-2.4, so the ~20 per cent variation of the MAST source is drawn as a full-height arch beside panels where the same vertical distance is a tenth of the scale. The three panels are presented as one comparison of where the source peaks; the independent autoscale reverses their apparent magnitudes. Either share a y-limit where the comparison is the point, or state on the MAST panel that it is on its own scale.

The one visible total-current trace on the MAST panel is clearly double-humped: a first maximum near radius 0.67 m, a minimum near 0.90 m and a second local maximum near 1.18 m. The run's record describes MAST 21978/35 as the converged control with a single maximum, and a reader will read this panel against that claim. With the reference and map traces invisible there is nothing on the panel to say whether the second hump belongs to the source or to the saved map, so the control claim cannot be checked from the figure.
